sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of "night" (that night and this night) are inverted between their supernal root and their lower manifestation, with "that night" above being higher than "this night," yet below it produces a greater concealment.

translations.translation: And based on this, there is additional explanation in that these two aspects of night
("that night" and "this night")
as they are below are in a manner opposite to how they are in their root,
for above, "that night" is higher than "this night," and as they are drawn below, the concealment
(for the worse)
of "that night" is a greater concealment than the concealment of "this night,"
for the two aspects of night that are above,
it can be said,
are the two aforementioned levels in the power of concealment of Ein Sof,
"this night" is the power of concealment
(night)
that relates to revelation
("this"),
and since the tzimtzum drawn from this level is for the sake of revelation,
therefore,
the night
(the concealment and hiding below)
is in a manner of "this,"
that it is felt in the revelation that it is night.
For this, that concealment brings about revelation, is specifically when the concealment is felt
[similar to the thirst for G‑dliness during the time of exile
(night)
which is greater than during the time of the Holy Temple,
which is the revelation that comes through the concealment,
and this is specifically through the concealment and hiding of the exile being felt].
And "that night" is the essence of the power of concealment that is above any relation to revelation,
for the tzimtzum drawn from this level is
(not for the sake of revelation,
but rather)
that in it the power of concealment is revealed,
and therefore the night below drawn from this aspect of tzimtzum is in a manner that it is not felt that it is concealment and hiding.
And the distinction between these two aspects in the service of man,
is,
that the service during night
(the darkness of exile,
and similarly the darkness of the entire physical world)
from the aspect of tzimtzum that is for the sake of revelation is the yearning and thirst to emerge from the darkness of night.
And the service during night from the aspect that in the tzimtzum the power of concealment is revealed is the contemplation etc. upon the root of the darkness of night itself,
whose root is in the essential concealment.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "that night" caused the sleep of the King to flee, because its lower root draws from the supernal "that night," and through Israel's mesirus nefesh during the year, this supernal aspect was drawn into the lower "that night."

translations.translation: And this is "on that night the sleep of the King fled," this is the King of the world,
for "that night" is what caused the sleep of the King to flee,
because the root of the lower "that night" is from the aspect of the supernal "that night,"
which is above the concealment of "that day" and even above the concealment of "this night."
And through Israel having stood then in mesirus nefesh throughout the entire year,
that their mesirus nefesh was from the aspect of concealment
[similar to what is explained elsewhere,
that during the time of exile the revelation of the power of mesirus nefesh is greater than during the time of the Holy Temple],
there was drawn
(in revelation)
the aspect of the supernal "that night" into the lower "that night."
And this is the connection of the two interpretations of "on that night the sleep of the King fled,"
that "that night" causes the matter of sleep
(and what is said "on that night the sleep of the King fled" is to emphasize the miracle,
that although it was on that night, nevertheless the sleep of the King fled)
and that "that night" caused the sleep of the King to flee,
for this, that "that night" causes the matter of sleep, is as it is in itself,
but through its root being drawn into it,
the aspect of the supernal "that night,"
then on the contrary,
it causes the sleep of the King to flee.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "the sleep of the King fled" is a level higher than even the supernal "that night," representing the union of concealment and revelation through the revelation of Atzmus, drawn by mesirus nefesh which comes from the essence of the soul.

translations.translation: And it should be added,
that "the sleep of the King fled" is above, even more than the supernal "that night"
[and "that night" is only a cause for the drawing down of "the sleep of the King fled"].
And the explanation is,
that day and night,
the power of concealment and the power of revelation in Ein Sof,
are two matters,
and therefore,
even after the drawing of the aspect of the supernal "that night" into the lower "that night,"
it remains night
[and even more,
"that night"],
for what is drawn into it is the power of concealment and not the power of revelation.
And similarly regarding this that they stood in mesirus nefesh throughout the entire year,
for since their mesirus nefesh came from the aspect of concealment
(as above in section 7),
that through the concealment the concealment of the soul that is above revelation is aroused,
this does not relate
(so much)
to the revealed powers,
and regarding the revealed powers they were
(even after the mesirus nefesh)
in a state of "that night."
And similar to what is explained in the maamar,
that this, that during sleep the superiority of one power over another is not discernible, is analogous to the powers as they are included in the essence of the soul,
where all the powers are in equality.
And from this it is understood,
that there is an advantage in sleep,
that specifically then the powers ascend to their source,
except that this advantage does not pertain to the revealed powers
(revelations),
and on the contrary,
in the revealed powers there is a deficiency and lack.
And this, that "on that night the sleep of the King fled,"
that "the sleep of the King fled" is the matter of the revelations drawn from this, that Ein Sof is below, below, without end
(the line of revelation),
it is the union of concealment and revelation.

And as explained in the aforementioned discourse of the Mitteler Rebbe, that this, that "on that night the sleep of the King fled," is like the parable of the deer with one eye open and one eye closed,
revelation and concealment together.
And he explains there,
that this, that there was then the union of the two opposites of concealment and revelation, is because then there was a revelation of Atzmus,
for regarding Atzmus,
concealment and revelation are not opposites.
And as explained elsewhere,
that this, that Atzmus has the ability to illuminate and the ability not to illuminate,
both are one matter.
And it can be said that what is stated in the maamar, that this, that "the sleep of the King fled" was brought about through the mesirus nefesh of Israel throughout the entire year,
the intention is also for the drawing down of Atzmus that occurred then,
for mesirus nefesh comes from the essence of the soul,
and therefore,
through mesirus nefesh they drew down Atzmus.
